# core/url.bastio

<!-- Generated by tests/libref.py from core/url.bastio: edit the source, then run tests/libref.py --write. -->

Percent-encoding (RFC 3986 section 2.1) and the query
string of a request target (`/path?a=1&b=two%20words`).

What is proved: no read is out of bounds, a decoded string is never longer
than the text it came from, an encoded one is at most three times as long,
and every byte the encoder writes is an unreserved character or a `%` with
two upper-case hex digits. Not proved: that decoding undoes encoding for
every input (the tests check it for all 256 byte values), or that the
query splitter agrees with any particular server's.

`import "core/url.bastio";` also loads [core/option.bastio](core-option.md), [core/bytes.bastio](core-bytes.md), [core/text.bastio](core-text.md), [core/num.bastio](core-num.md).

| Function | |
| --- | --- |
| [`url_encode`](#url_encode) | `b` percent-encoded for use as a URL component. |
| [`url_decode_span`](#url_decode_span) | The bytes `from..to` of `b` with each `%XX` replaced by the byte it names, and, when `plus` is true, each `+` by a space (the form of a query string). |
| [`url_decode`](#url_decode) | All of `b` percent-decoded (see `url_decode_span`). |
| [`url_query_start`](#url_query_start) | The index of the first `?` in `b`, or `blen(b)` if there is none. |
| [`url_query_get`](#url_query_get) | The decoded value of the first parameter named `key` in the query string that starts at byte `from` of `b` (`a=1&b=two+words`), with `+` read as a space. |

Every example below is built, verified and run by `tests/run.sh`. An `assert` in one is proved at compile time from the contracts above it.

## Functions

### `url_encode`

```bastio
fn url_encode(b: &Bytes) -> Bytes
  ensures blen(result) >= blen(b) && blen(result) <= 3 * blen(b)
```

`b` percent-encoded for use as a URL component: letters, digits and
`-._~` stay, every other byte becomes `%` and two upper-case hex digits.

Example:

```bastio
let b = bfrom("a b&c=é");
let e = url_encode(b);
let ok = bytes_eq_str(e, "a%20b%26c%3D%C3%A9");
bfree(e);
bfree(b);
if !ok { return 1; }
```

### `url_decode_span`

```bastio
fn url_decode_span(b: &Bytes, from: u64, to: u64, plus: bool) -> Option[Bytes]
  requires from <= to && to <= blen(b)
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> blen(result.Some) <= to - from
```

The bytes `from..to` of `b` with each `%XX` replaced by the byte it names,
and, when `plus` is true, each `+` by a space (the form of a query
string). `None` when a `%` is not followed by two hex digits inside the
span.

Example:

```bastio
let b = bfrom("x=a%20b+c%2b");
let mut ok = false;
match url_decode_span(b, 2, 12, true) {
  Option::Some(v) => { ok = bytes_eq_str(v, "a b c+"); bfree(v); },
  Option::None => {},
}
let cut = bfrom("100%");
let mut refused = true;
match url_decode_span(cut, 0, 4, false) {
  Option::Some(v) => { refused = false; bfree(v); },
  Option::None => {},
}
bfree(b);
bfree(cut);
if !ok || !refused { return 1; }
```

### `url_decode`

```bastio
fn url_decode(b: &Bytes, plus: bool) -> Option[Bytes]
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> blen(result.Some) <= blen(b)
```

All of `b` percent-decoded (see `url_decode_span`).

Example:

```bastio
let b = bfrom("%E2%82%AC5");
let mut ok = false;
match url_decode(b, false) {
  Option::Some(v) => { ok = blen(v) == 4 && bget(v, 0) == 226 && bget(v, 3) == 53; bfree(v); },
  Option::None => {},
}
bfree(b);
if !ok { return 1; }
```

### `url_query_start`

```bastio
fn url_query_start(b: &Bytes) -> u64
  ensures result <= blen(b)
```

The index of the first `?` in `b`, or `blen(b)` if there is none: the
path of a request target is `0..url_query_start(b)` and the query string
starts one byte later.

Example:

```bastio
let t = bfrom("/todos?done=1");
let n = bfrom("/todos");
let q = url_query_start(t);
let none = url_query_start(n);
bfree(t);
bfree(n);
if q != 6 || none != 6 { return 1; }
```

### `url_query_get`

```bastio
fn url_query_get(b: &Bytes, from: u64, key: Str) -> Option[Bytes]
  requires from <= blen(b)
```

The decoded value of the first parameter named `key` in the query string
that starts at byte `from` of `b` (`a=1&b=two+words`), with `+` read as a
space. A parameter with no `=` has the value "". `None` when there is no
such parameter or its value is not valid percent-encoding. The key is
compared as written, so a key that is itself encoded does not match.

Example:

```bastio
let t = bfrom("/s?q=a+b%21&n=7&flag");
let mut q = false;
let mut n = false;
let mut f = false;
match url_query_get(t, 3, "q") { Option::Some(v) => { q = bytes_eq_str(v, "a b!"); bfree(v); }, Option::None => {} }
match url_query_get(t, 3, "n") { Option::Some(v) => { n = bytes_eq_str(v, "7"); bfree(v); }, Option::None => {} }
match url_query_get(t, 3, "flag") { Option::Some(v) => { f = blen(v) == 0; bfree(v); }, Option::None => {} }
let mut found = false;
match url_query_get(t, 3, "x") { Option::Some(v) => { found = true; bfree(v); }, Option::None => {} }
bfree(t);
if !q || !n || !f || found { return 1; }
```

## Internals

### `url_unreserved`

```bastio
fn url_unreserved(c: u8) -> bool
```

Internal: `c` needs no escaping in a URL component: a letter, a digit,
or one of `-`, `.`, `_`, `~`.

### `url_hex_up`

```bastio
fn url_hex_up(d: u64) -> u8
  requires d < 16
```

Internal: the upper-case hex digit for `d`.
